A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DeepCrossAttention and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H. Corresponding content can be matched despite the layout changes and substantive additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic linear-network experiments, LM1B and C4 evaluations, scaling studies, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original language-modeling and synthetic experiments, plus ImageNet classification, additional C4 comparisons, and a model-input ablation.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same GRN-v1/v2/v3 procedures, three independent GRN-v3 instances for attention inputs, and first-and-last-k approximation. ImageNet applies the existing method; the new GRN-v3 theory does not introduce an algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v2 adds ImageNet image classification to the synthetic and LM1B/C4 language-modeling tasks retained from v1. This introduces a distinct modality and task, extending evaluation beyond language modeling.

E2.justification: For the already-covered C4 task, v2 Table 6 adds LAuReL-PA, 1x1-DenseFormer, and Hyper-Connections comparisons beyond v1's transformer-versus-8-DCA evaluation. Hyper-Connections is evaluated with stack sizes 4 and 10. The LM1B comparator set remains unchanged, including dynamic Hyper-Connections despite its shortened table label.

E3.justification: The reported Table 2 width-scaling setting changes from 24 layers to 12 layers, preventing direct same-setting score comparisons. New protocols include ViT-S/16 classification measured by loss and accuracy, and a six-layer GRN-v3 control comparing the last four outputs with the model input plus the last three. The existing language-model training budget and optimizer settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds Table 9, referenced in Appendix H, testing whether explicitly retaining the model input helps GRN-v3. Width sensitivity is reevaluated at a different reported depth, and the existing component ablation receives revised results. The earlier efficiency, stability, retrofitting, and learned-weight analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Tables 1, 2, 4, 5, and 7 in v2 add plus/minus uncertainty entries where v1 reported point values, and Figure 6 adds shaded ranges. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting, but the PDFs do not specify the statistic represented, run counts, or seeds; additional runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: Several LM1B tables and Figure 6 change numerically. In Table 5, DCA changes from 17.998 to 18.06±0.01 and Hyper-Connections from 18.633 to 18.65±0.03, reducing the reported gap from 0.635 to 0.59. New results include C4 perplexities of 20.392 for 8-DCA versus 20.718 for the best listed competitor, ImageNet accuracies of 76.4 versus 77.1, and Table 9 perplexities of 20.301 versus 20.227 without versus with the model input. Table 2 results use a changed depth; Table 3 is unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 extends Theorems 4.1–4.3, Proposition 4.4, and Lemma C.1 to GRN-v3, with substantial new proofs in Appendices A–D and a Gaussian/ReLU moment lemma. These add expressivity, risk, and parameter-budget guarantees beyond v1's GRN-v1/v2 analysis. The new Lemma B.1 contains an arithmetic inconsistency affecting the subsequent bound derivation.

C1.justification: The introduction expands the empirical contribution claim from language modeling and perplexity to include image classification and accuracy. The abstract's up-to-3x training-speed claim and the core efficiency, parameter-count, and stability claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 extends the task-complexity, collective-rank, and input-dimension interpretations to GRN-v3. Section 5 interprets the new ImageNet result as evidence of applicability to vision. Existing memory-overhead qualifications and the early-training exception in Appendix F are retained.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new vision experiment's ViT-S/16 architecture and 22M parameter count and identifies Beyer et al. (2022) as its setup reference. The added comparisons specify Hyper-Connections stack sizes and GRN-v3 input selections. Existing optimizer, hardware, and language-training details are retained; no code-access change is reported.

R1.justification: v2 adds Highway networks and Srivastava et al. (2015) to the residual-network history, and cites Beyer et al. (2022) for the vision experiment. The positioning relative to DenseFormer, LAuReL, and Hyper-Connections otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The section and appendix sequence and most existing prose are retained. Local revisions expand descriptions and cross-references, add acknowledgments, update author information, and change citation style; there is no extensive narrative reorganization.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column layout to an ICML two-column layout, substantially resizing and repositioning figures and tables. v2 adds Tables 6, 8, and 9, renumbers the original ablation table to Table 7, adds shaded ranges to Figure 6, and reformats several tables for uncertainty entries.

improvement.justification: The added C4 comparisons, ImageNet evaluation, and model-input ablation strengthen empirical support. However, the new GRN-v3 theory has a concrete reliability problem: Lemma B.1 combines 3/2 and (d−1)/2 as (d+1)/2 rather than (d+2)/2, and this constant feeds the new risk bounds. The added uncertainty values also lack definitions and run counts. The empirical gains and unresolved problems in the theoretical extension prevent a confident net quality judgment.
